10390.author: cms-sw
10390.body:
This PR proposes to build Torch separately for `cpu, cuda and rocm`. For now torch-rocm is not enabled as it requires full distribution of rocm (nearly 11GB)[a]. We should be able to build most/all of [a] from sources using https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries . 

For now this PR proposes to split torch in cpu and cuda part as a proof of concept that we can dynamically select env depending on available resources. Currently this PR proposes the following
- `py3-torch`: Only cpu c++ API and python interface
- `py3-torch-cuda`: cuda and cpu  c++ API and python interface
- `py3-torch-<extensions>` (e.g. `cluster`, `scatter` and `sparse`): cpu only python interface
- `py3-torch-<extensions>-cuda` (e.g. `cluster`, `scatter` and `sparse`): cuda and cpu python interface

As we do not have `py3-torch-rocm` yet ( which needs full 11GB of rocm distribution), on amdgpu hosts we fall back to cpu only interface. SCRAM will dynamically set the env e.g. on
- cpu only host:
  - LD_LIBRARY_PATH: `<path>/lib`
  - PYTHON3PATH:`<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages`
- host with cuda:
  - LD_LIBRARY_PATH: `<path>/lib/scram_cuda:<path>/lib`(where <path>/lib/scram_cuda contains libs for cuda and cpu torch)
  - PYTHON3PATH: `<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/scram_cuda:<path>/lib/python3.12/site-packages`

for rocm, for now we fall back to cpu only libs/python modules.

I also have added triton and aotriton spec so that if we have to build the torch-rocm fully from sources then we can use aotirton. For now torch-rocm downloads prebuild aotriton bundle at build time

This need https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw-config/pull/117 too

[a]
```
 hipblas-common-devel
  miopen-hip miopen-hip-devel
  hipfft hipfft-devel
  hipsparse hipsparse-devel
  rocprim-devel hipcub-devel
  rocthrust-devel
  hipsolver hipsolver-devel
  rocsolver  rocsolver-devel
  hipblaslt hipblaslt-devel
  hipsparselt hipsparselt-devel
  roctrace roctrac-devel
  rocblas rocblas-devel
```

10848.author: cms-sw
10848.body:
GCC 15 can use excessive memory when compiling some macro-heavy CMSSW sources. For example, RecoTracker/LSTCore/src/alpaka/LST.cc uses ~9 GB of memory, with most of it spent during preprocessing/macro-expansion tracking. This can lead to OOM failures when multiple compilation jobs run in parallel.

Testing -ftrack-macro-expansion=0 reduces the memory usage of this compilation from ~9 GB to below 1 GB and also reduces the compilation time significantly.

This PR enables -ftrack-macro-expansion=0 to evaluate its impact on CMSSW builds. The option only disables detailed macro-expansion tracking for diagnostics; macro expansion and generated code are unchanged.

If the test is successful, we will consider enabling it for IB/release builds while retaining full macro-expansion tracking for CI/PR builds.
10848.title: [GCC15] Add -ftrack-macro-expansion=0 to avoid high RSS during pre-processing

10863.body:
* Re-acquire jobserver tokens periodically.

The wrapper asks for tokens at startup, and then again every `HIPCC_PARALLEL_JOBSERVER_RETRY` seconds (default 10), for as long as there is still an architecture waiting for a slot.

* Support the new offloading driver.

`--offload-new-driver` packages the per-architecture bitcode instead of bundling it, so the wrapper fell back to a serial compile. Detect the pipeline from -### and split it too. The host compile now runs after the packager rather than alongside the device compiles, since it consumes their output.  The new driver can parallelise also the LTO linking step.

Enable the new offload compiler driver and disable LTO partitions:

The new offload driver can run multiple device LTO compilations in parallel.
Together with LTO partitions this could end up using more processes than requested by the jobserver.

LTO partitions have also been reported to result in a potential performance loss over 10%.

Both options are expected to be the new default in ROCm 10.1.

49555.body:
#### PR description

This PR extends the L1TGlobal AXOL1TL support to allow proper monitoring and offline validation of the AXOL1TL anomaly-detection (AD) trigger.

Specifically, it introduces the following functionality:

- Adds storage of **all AXOL1TL neural-network input features** inside `AXOL1TLScore`, together with a public accessor method.
- Adds recording of the **per-event input vector used by the emulator** (`m_lastInputs_`) inside `AXOL1TLCondition`, enabling downstream ntuple production and debugging.
- Updates `AXOL1TLCondition` to fill `m_lastInputs_` during `evaluateCondition()`.
- Extends the L1TNtuples plugin `L1AXOTreeProducer` to:
  - write a new branch `axo_inputs[57]` containing the full input vector,
  - write the `axo_score` as before,
  - ensure consistent branch filling even when the product is missing.
- Ensures that the AXOL1TL input dimensionality is expressed through a single constant (`kNInputs`) and is used consistently across all classes.

No changes are expected to physics outputs of any existing L1T algorithms.  
This PR only affects debug/monitoring structures and ntuple content.

This PR does not depend on other open PRs or external packages.

---

#### PR validation

Validation steps performed:

1. **CMSSW compiles successfully** with `scram b -j 8` in a fresh `CMSSW_16_0_X` area.
2. A RAWDIGI L1T emulation configuration was run using:
   ```
   cmsDriver.py l1Ntuple -s RAW2DIGI --python_filename=data.py -n -1 --data        --conditions=140X_dataRun3_v20 --era=Run3        --customise=L1Trigger/Configuration/customiseReEmul.L1TReEmulFromRAW        --customise=L1Trigger/L1TNtuples/customiseL1Ntuple.L1NtupleRAWEMU        --filein=/path/to/RAW --fileout=L1Ntuple.root
   ```
3. The resulting ntuple was inspected manually; the new branches  
   - `axo_score`  
   - `axo_inputs[57]`  
   are present and contain the expected placeholder values when the score product is missing.
4. The tree structure and branch types were verified by scanning the ntuple in ROOT.
5. A standalone analysis script using `ROOT.RDataFrame` was used to read and plot all new branches, confirming correct storage and array dimensionality.

No changes to runTheMatrix outputs are expected, as this code is only exercised when the L1TNtuples workflow is explicitly enabled.

---

#### Backport

This PR is **not** a backport.

If backports are requested, it would be appropriate for the Run-3 production cycles (13_2_X, 14_0_X), as the changes affect monitoring and offline validation of the AXOL1TL trigger.

---

#### Checklist reminder (for submission)

- [x] PR targets the correct branch  
- [ ] Code follows CMS Naming, Coding & Style Rules  
- [ ] PR passes the basic tests described in the CMSSW PR instructions

#### PR description:

This PR adds the following changes to NNvtx models:

- Weight, pattern, and association [tensorflow models](https://github.com/cms-data/L1Trigger-L1TTrackMatch/pull/4) have been replaced by hls4ml, including updates to emulator to match model quantization of QKeras training
- NN weight replaces pT in the output VertexWord when running NN vertexing (before: only vertex field filled)

HW tests have shown 100% agreement with this new emulation. The new vertex bin tiebreak procedure has shown equal or better performance in emulation, with better timing performance on HW. 51458.body: **PR description:** This PR introduces a `SoAMultiView`. The `SoAMultiView` holds an `std::array` of `ConstViews` and keeps track of the valid range of each view. It can be seen as the equivalent to the [MultiSpan](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/DataFormats/Common/interface/MultiSpan.h) for SoAs. The range of each view can be user-defined; by default, the `view.metadata().size()` is taken. The `SoAMultiView` is useful if `PortableCollections` templated on the same SoA-Layout from multiple producers forms a single iteration space in downstream algorithms. Due to the design of using a fixed-sized array to hold the `ConstViews` it is possible to pass an `SoAMultiView` to a kernel by value like a `ConstView` is usually passed to a kernel. This makes the `SoAMultiView` a drop-in replacement for kernels that use a single `ConstView`. Also, this PR uses the `SoAMultiView` in the CA instead of [SiPixelRecHitExtendedAlpaka](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelRecHits/plugins/alpaka/SiPixelRecHitExtendedAlpaka.cc) that copies the data of two `PortableCollections` to a single `PortableCollection`. With the `SoAMultiView` the copy routine is fully replaced. ## Timing Measurements run on 2x AMD EPYC 9534 with 4x L40 GPUs. 51868.body:
#### PR description:

In https://indico.cern.ch/event/1716929/#17-cosmic-background-for-run-3
on slide13 the analyzers reported a muon duplication for cosmics data.

`MuonIdProducer` can emit two `reco::Muon` with a **identical four-vector** for a single tracker track, because both take their momentum from the same `innerTrack`. The DisMuon analysis sees this in **20.7%** of two-muon cosmic MC events and **17.7%** of NoBPTX data events in `slimmedDisplacedMuons`.

There are two mechanisms:

1. A tracker track that crosses the interaction point is propagated in **both** directions (so that both hemispheres of muon chambers are reachable), and each propagation builds its own muon.
2. The "already in the list" test can fail between a global muon and its own tracker candidate on a **non-crossing** traversing track, because the test compares the $\phi$ of the muon interaction regions and the two legs land in opposite hemispheres.

This PR adds a `mergeCrossingTrackLegs` parameter. When it is on, the tracker-muon loop builds **one** merged candidate for an IP-crossing track, holding the chamber matches of both propagation directions de-duplicated by chamber `DetId`, and the "already in the list" test keys on **`innerTrack` identity alone** rather than on the $\phi$ test. Opposite-hemisphere merges fill the existing muon's own leg first, so no chamber match is lost.

**Defaults are deliberately asymmetric.** `muons1stStep_cfi.py` sets the parameter **`True`**, so offline reconstruction gets the fix. The `fillDescriptions` default stays **`False`**, and the `MuonIdProducer` instances in the HLT menus do not set the parameter, so **HLT is unchanged by construction**. 

Note that `muons1stStep_cfi.py` must carry the parameter explicitly: `desc.setAllowAnything()` means the `fillDescriptions` default is never injected into the hand-written cfi, so `clone()` would otherwise raise `TypeError: mergeCrossingTrackLegs does not already exist`.

#### PR validation:

**Offline, from the same `step2.root` in each A/B pair**

| sample | setup | result |
|---|---|---|
| cosmics relval 7.3 | flag off | identical to baseline |
| cosmics relval 7.3 | default on | `muons` 2  **0** duplicate groups, `splitMuons` 1  0, `muons1Leg` 3  0 |
| DY relval 16850.0 (`-w upgrade`) | default on, incl. `earlyMuons` | **identical** to flag off |

A "duplicate group" is one tracker track that produced more than one `reco::Muon`, bucketed by the `innerTrack` `(product id, key)`.

`splitMuons` is included on purpose: it has the same *within-leg* duplicates, so "splitMuons already gives per-leg muons" does not rescue it. The two *genuine* legs of a split muon have distinct `innerTrack` refs and are never merged.

**`runTheMatrix.py -l limited`**: all **33/33** non-data workflows pass, including `7.3 CosmicsSPLoose2018`. 

**HLT.** The `fillDescriptions` default of `False` is load-bearing. Running the GRun menu twice over identical events at `nThreads=1`, once stock and once with `mergeCrossingTrackLegs=True` forced on all 12 instances, and comparing every path's accept bit plus every muon:

| sample | events | pairs sharing one `innerTrack` (off  on) | events differing | trigger decisions changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NoBPTX Run2023B (data) | 5000 | 12  **0** | 5 | **1** |
| RelValTTbarToDilepton_14TeV (Run3 MC) | 1500 | 0  0 | 0 | 0 |

So the fix removes every one-track duplicate at HLT and creates none: but in one NoBPTX event it also flips **nine jet paths** (`HLT_AK8PFJet40`, `AlCa_AK8PFJet40`, `MC_PFHT`, `MC_AK4PFJets`, `MC_AK8PFJets`, `MC_AK8PFHT`) and, importantly, the **dataset assignments** `Dataset_JetMET0`, `Dataset_JetMET1`, `Dataset_AlCaLowPtJet`. `hltMuons` feeds HLT particle flow, so a duplicated 98 GeV muon is double-counted into PF jets and HT; merging it removes the phantom energy and the event drops below threshold. The direction is arguably the correct physics, but it is a jet-trigger rate change and a stream-routing change, ~~so it is left to a follow-up under TSG review rather than being taken here.~~

EDIT: After the comments from Marco, I've changed the default here too.

The effect is confined to cosmic-like topologies: the merge requires an IP-crossing or opposite-hemisphere track. The $t\bar{t}$ sample carries more muons per event (1.13 vs 0.65) and shows no differences at all. The NoBPTX number is therefore an upper bound rather than a menu-wide rate, and it rests on a single event.

#### PR description:

This PR is removing the non-extended Patatrack configuration for HLT Phase-2. This includes the procModifier `hltPhase2LegacyTrackingPatatrackQuads` that activates the tracking variant, all its custom HLT module configurations, and the related runTheMatrix workflow.

At the moment, there are two legacy tracking configurations supported for HLT Phase-2:
- **`hltPhase2LegacyTracking`** : Legacy HLT tracking from the TDR (2 iterations of Legacy Pixel Seeds + CKF).
- **`hltPhase2LegacyTrackingPatatrackQuads`** : same as previous, but replaces the seeding of the first iteration by (non-OT-extended) Patatrack pixel tracks.

Both legacy configurations are not actively used for development but instead are mainly kept as a reference baseline. They show very similar performance physics-wise (see [comparison validation plots here](https://jaschulz.web.cern.ch/Plots/TrackingPOG/procModifiersSep26/TTbar_200PU/LegacyComparison/)), and are largely outperformed by the current default HLT tracking in most phase-spaces. Due to the similar physics performance, keeping one as a reference should be sufficient. The choice to keep the "legacy" Legacy one is based on the fact that it is still frequently used as a reference in DP notes and internal meetings. 
Removing "Patatrack" Legacy simplifies maintenance and the integration of new developments. It also is in line with the efforts to reduce the number of unneeded procModifiers in the HLT menu as discussed in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/51817 and as followed-up in the [HLT Upgrade meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1726810/).

51917.author: mmusich
51917.body:
#### PR description:

In view of subsequent work for Phase-2 alignment, this PR introduces `FastDMRChecker`, a new lightweight `EDAnalyzer` for computing DMRs/DRnRs (and by-layer/by-disk residual-pull histograms) without the full overhead of `DMRChecker`. Also factors the code shared between the two into a new header-only library, `interface/DMRHelper.h`.

**New: `plugins/FastDMRChecker.cc`**
- Computes DMRs, DRnRs, and split-DMRs for BPix/FPix/TIB/TOB/TID/TEC.
- Also books by-(subdet, layer/disk) residual and pull histograms across all six subdetectors, using `findSubdetAndLayer()` + a lazily-booked `HistoSet`.

**New: `interface/DMRHelper.h`**
- Shared `Estimators`/`EstimatorMap`/`updateOnlineMomenta()` (running mean/variance), `findSubdetAndLayer()`, `fillByLayer()`, `bookSplitDMRHistograms()`.
- Binning differences between `FastDMRChecker` and `DMRChecker` expressed via a `Traits` template parameter (`DefaultDMRBinning` / `FullDMRBinning`) rather than duplicated functions.

**`plugins/DMRChecker.cc`:** migrated onto `DMRHelper.h` for the pieces that were exact duplicates (`running` namespace, `updateOnlineMomenta`, `bookSplitDMRHistograms`, `cmToUm`). Its `bookResidualsHistogram()`/`fillByIndex()` (pixel-only, pre-booked, with clamping) were left untouched since they behave differently from `fillByLayer()`  no functional change to `DMRChecker`'s existing output.


#### PR validation:

- [x] Ran existing `DMRChecker`/`FastDMRChecker` test cfg(s) on a small sample, diffed output histograms against `master` for `DMRChecker` (expect no diff)
- [x] Confirmed new `FastDMRChecker` by-layer histograms are populated/sane
- [x] Grepped for other users of removed symbols (`running::`, member `bookSplitDMRHistograms`/`updateOnlineMomenta`/`findSubdetAndLayer`)

51924.author: mmusich
51924.body:
#### PR description:

This PR removes every dependence of the Phase-2 HLT menus (`HLT_75e33_cff`, `HLT_75e33_timing_cff`, `HLT_NGTScouting_cff`, and therefore `HLT_75e33_trackingOnly_cff`) on EventSetup configuration fragments owned by the offline reconstruction packages. Until now the menus loaded ~40 `cfi`/`cff` files from `RecoTracker`, `RecoLocalTracker`, `RecoLocalCalo`, `TrackingTools`, `TrackPropagation`, `RecoJets` and `CalibMuon`, so that any change made there for offline reconstruction silently changed the HLT menu as well. The menus now only load `Configuration/StandardSequences/Accelerators_cff` and the HLT-owned fragments in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_75e33/eventsetup/`, as the Run-3 menus do.

Details:
- Every `ESProducer`/`ESSource` previously pulled in from RECO is now defined in its own `cfi` under `HLT_75e33/eventsetup/`, with the parameters it has in the Phase-2 menu once the era modifiers are applied (e.g. `phase2_tracker`, `trackingPhase2PU140`, `phase2_hgcal`, `run2_HCAL_2017`). The four HLT-owned fragments that were never loaded (`hltESPMeasurementTracker`, `hltESPRKTrajectoryFitter`, `hltESPRKTrajectorySmoother`, `hltESPKFFittingSmootherWithOutliersRejectionAndRK`) were updated to the Phase-2 values and are now used; `hltESPGlobalDetLayerGeometry` is loaded as is.
- Module labels and `ComponentName`s use the Run-3 HLT naming (`hltESP*`, `hltESS*`) wherever the product is only referenced from the configuration, and all consumers (modules and PSets) are updated accordingly, e.g. `WithTrackAngle`  `hltESPTTRHBuilderWithTrackAngle`, `PixelCPEGeneric`  `hltESPPixelCPEGeneric`, `FlexibleKFFittingSmoother`  `hltESPFlexibleKFFittingSmoother`, `MeasurementTracker` (empty `ComponentName`)  `hltESPMeasurementTracker`. The four tracking components with offline names already present in the menu (`initialStepChi2Est`, `highPtTripletStepChi2Est`, `highPtTripletStepTrajectoryCleanerBySharedHits`, `muonSeededTrajectoryCleanerBySharedHits`) get the `hlt` prefix too.
- Five RECO modules were identical to HLT ones already in the menu and are merged into them (`ttrhbwr`, `KFUpdatorESProducer`, `RungeKuttaTrackerPropagator`, `pixelTrackCleanerBySharedHits`, `fwdGsfElectronPropagator`). Six modules that the RECO `cfi`s define only as a side effect of their imports and that nothing in the menu references are dropped (`clusterShapeHitFilterESProducer`, `tkTransientTrackingRecHitBuilderESProducer`, `navigationSchoolESProducerParabolicMf`, `TTRHBuilderFast`, `RKFittingSmoother`, `PropagatorWithMaterialForLoopersOpposite`).
- 20 modules keep their offline label and `ComponentName` on purpose: `SteppingHelixPropagatorAny`, `TransientTrackBuilderESProducer`, `ClusterShapeHitFilterESProducer`, `AnyDirectionAnalyticalPropagator`, `MaterialPropagator`, `OppositeMaterialPropagator`, `MaterialPropagatorParabolicMF`, `navigationSchoolESProducer`, the six `*DetIdAssociator`s, and the producers whose product carries no data label (`CSCChannelMapperESProducer`, `CSCIndexerESProducer`, `CaloTowerConstituentsMapBuilder`, `ecalSeverityLevel`, `hcalRecAlgos`, `hcalChannelPropertiesESProd`). Their product names are hardcoded in C++ (e.g. `MuonIdProducer`, `TrackAssociatorParameters`, `ClusterShapeTrajectoryFilter`, `CkfTrackCandidateMakerBase`, `SeedFromProtoTrack`, the b-tagging and vertexing plugins) or are the defaults of parameters a configuration may leave unset, so the product cannot be renamed; and a module delivering the same product as an offline one has to carry the same label, otherwise the two conflict (`EventSetupConflict`) whenever the HLT fragment runs in the same process as the DIGI or RECO sequences. This is the same set of exceptions the Run-3 menus have.
- `hltESPPhase2StripCPE` delivers its product as `Phase2StripCPEHLT` (via `appendToDataLabel`, since `ComponentType` fixes both the plugin and the product label), so it does not clash with the offline `phase2StripCPEESProducer`.
- `hltMeasurementTrackerEvent` drops the Run-2/3 `siStripDigis` inactive-strip label and the unset `mightGet`.

No change is expected in the HLT results: the configuration is identical to the previous one up to the renaming of EventSetup products described above. The labels of EventSetup modules in the HLT configuration dumps change, so customisations referring to the old offline labels (e.g. `process.MeasurementTracker`, `process.ttrhbwr`) need to be updated.

No dependence on other PRs or externals.

#### PR validation:

- The full configuration of the four menus was dumped (`dumpPython` of every `ESProducer`/`ESSource`, `EDProducer`/`EDFilter`/`EDAnalyzer` and top-level `PSet`) before and after the change, with the `Phase2C17I13M9` and `Phase2C26I13M9` eras: after applying the intended rename map, the 93 EventSetup modules, 712 ED modules and 38 PSets are identical, and the four menus carry identical EventSetup content.
- Every renamed product name was checked against a scan of all quoted string literals in the C++ sources at the base commit, to make sure no plugin fetches it by a hardcoded name.
- `cmsRun` of the Phase-2 HLT step (`DIGI,...,HLT:75e33`) [`ph2_hlt` matrix] runs successfully.

51927.body: #### PR description: A patch for updating the L1 seed used in the Phase-2 `HLT_Photon187` path. The goal is to migrate the L1 seed filtering from the current `L1TTkEmFilter` implementation to the P2GT-based filtering. The new filter uses the `pSingleEGEle51` algorithm from `l1tGTAlgoBlockProducer` for the single photon L1 seed. #### Description of the current changes: The updates include: * Adding `hltEGL1SeedsForSinglePhotonNonIsolatedFilter`, using `HLTP2GTSingleObjectFilter` with the `pSingleEGEle51` P2GT algorithm and `CL2Photons` collection. * Replacing `l1tTkEmSingle51Filter` with the new P2GT-based L1 seed filter in both `HLTPhoton187L1SeededSequence` and `HLTPhoton187UnseededSequence`. * Removing the corresponding `l1tTkEmSingle51Filter` configuration, which is no longer used by the `HLT_Photon187` sequences. #### PR validation: The PR has been prepared starting from `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100`: ```bash cmsrel CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100 cd CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100/src cmsenv git cms-init git cms-addpkg HLTrigger/Configuration scram b && scram b code-checks && scram b code-format && scram b ``` #### Phase-2 HLT validation: The HLT efficiencies before and after the PR were compared as a function of $p_T$ in the barrel region using sample `/RelValZEE_14/CMSSW_20_0_0-PU_150X_mcRun4_realistic_v1_STD_D121_RegeneratedGS_PU_16Aug26-v6/GEN-SIM-RECO` under geometry `ExtendedRun4D121`, and no significant difference was observed.
